events.title: Newton Publishes the Principia Mathematica
events.description: Isaac Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was published in London under the auspices of the Royal Society, with the support of Edmond Halley. The work set out the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation.
events.significance: It laid the foundations of classical mechanics and transformed scientific understanding of the physical universe for over two centuries.

events.title: Venezuela Declares Independence from Spain
events.description: The Congress of Venezuela formally adopted a declaration of independence, making Venezuela one of the first Spanish American colonies to break from Spanish rule.
events.significance: It was a key step in the Spanish American wars of independence and is celebrated annually as Venezuela's Independence Day.

events.title: The Salvation Army Is Founded
events.description: William Booth and his wife Catherine founded the Christian Mission in the East End of London, which was later renamed The Salvation Army in 1878.
events.significance: It grew into one of the world's largest charitable and humanitarian organizations, providing aid to the poor and homeless in over 130 countries.

events.title: The National Health Service Is Launched in the United Kingdom
events.description: The NHS began operating, offering healthcare free at the point of use to all UK residents. The service was championed by Health Minister Aneurin Bevan.
events.significance: It became a model for public healthcare systems worldwide and remains a central institution in British society.

events.title: Dolly the Sheep Is Born
events.description: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, was born at the Roslin Institute in Scotland. Her existence was announced publicly in February 1997.
events.significance: Her birth demonstrated that adult cells could be reprogrammed, sparking major advances in biotechnology and ethical debates about cloning.
